t: Uzbekistan declared independence on 31 August 1991 after the failed coup in Moscow, and Islam Karimov, Communist first secretary since 1989, ruled it as an authoritarian president until his death in September 2016.

The economy rests on commodities: in 2011 Uzbekistan was the world's seventh-largest producer and fifth-largest exporter of cotton and its seventh-largest gold producer, while Soviet-era plants and ample gas make it the largest electricity producer in Central Asia.

Shavkat Mirziyoyev, president from December 2016, made the currency fully convertible in September 2017, abolished Soviet-style exit visas and mended relations with every neighbour, though V-Dem still classed the state a closed autocracy in 2024.
dyk: Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world, the other being Liechtenstein: none of its rivers reaches the sea, and the Aral Sea on its northern edge, once the fourth-largest inland sea on Earth, has shrunk to about a tenth of its former area since the 1960s.
ev: Uzbekistan declares independence on 31 August after the failed coup in Moscow; Islam Karimov is elected president on 29 December.
The Oliy Majlis replaces the Supreme Soviet, the Republican Stock Exchange opens and Uzbekistan applies to join the World Trade Organization.
After the 11 September attacks Uzbekistan grants the United States access to the Karshi-Khanabad airfield for operations in Afghanistan.
Government troops fire into crowds of protesters in Andijan, killing 187 by official count and several hundred by witness accounts; the United States is ordered to leave Karshi-Khanabad.
The Afrosiyob high-speed train between Tashkent and Samarkand, the first in Central Asia, makes its first trip on 26 August.
Karimov dies on 2 September; Prime Minister Shavkat Mirziyoyev is elected president with 88.6 percent of the vote and sworn in on 14 December.
In September the som becomes fully convertible at market rates, ending the chief barrier to foreign business.
The United Nations announces 'major progress' against forced labour in the cotton harvest, with 94 percent of pickers working voluntarily.

f.founder: Islam Karimov, first secretary of the Communist Party of Uzbekistan from 1989, elected president of independent Uzbekistan on 29 December 1991
f.predecessor: Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic (Soviet Union), created on 27 October 1924
